To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MedScan is a useful and accurate tool for extracting information from biomedical abstracts.
MedScan is a natural language processing (NLP) engine for the biomedical literature that performs well in a variety of tasks.

MedScan is able to extract the main concepts from MEDLINE abstracts with high precision and recall, that it is able to extract a large number of relations between concepts with high precision, that it is robust to spelling errors and to the presence of abbreviations, that it is capable of dealing with complex sentences, that it is fast enough to be useful in a production environment, and that the results are useful for the end-user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MedScan, a natural-language-processing system for MEDLINE abstract processing.
developing and applying natural language processing techniques for processing MEDLINE abstracts and other text sources.
the development of MedScan, a system for extracting relevant information from the MEDLINE database of biomedical research papers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MedScan is a useful tool for extracting structured information from MEDLINE abstracts, but it is not yet a reliable and accurate tool for the purpose.
MedScan has been shown to perform well on a variety of tasks, but the performance is not yet at a level that can be used in clinical practice.
the MedScan system is a very useful tool for the automatic indexing of biomedical literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed MedScan, a natural-language-processing system for the automatic extraction of information from biomedical abstracts.

MedScan is the first natural language processing (NLP) engine that can automatically process MEDLINE abstracts, and extract and represent their main content in a form that can be used by a variety of downstream applications.
we developed an automatic text processing system for biomedical literature that is capable of extracting information from the text.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the performance of a NLP system is highly dependent on the task, the same is true for the quality of the training set.
, for a wide variety of NLP tasks, it is beneficial to train a model on multiple languages.
the use of natural language processing (NLP) techniques to identify relevant literature is not only feasible but also very effective.
